newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close higher on dry weather concerns.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close higher on dry weather concerns.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed higher on a correction from Wednesday's steep slide with weather forecasts for the Midwest also viewed as supportive, traders said.
"We need rain and we're not getting it plus it was overdone (oversold) yesterday," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.

Midday weather reports indicated little chance of significant rain in the eastern U.S. soybean growing region. Early this week there were some outlooks for crop-enhancing moisture in the Midwest on the remnants of Hurricane Fran.

Also Wednesday's National Weather Service six- to 10-day forecast was for below normal temperatures and normal to below normal rainfall for nearly all key U.S. soybean growing region from September 10 through September 14.
"The six- to 10-day was cool and dry and what it needs (soy crop) is warm and wet," said Vic Lespinasse of Dean Witter Reynolds.
Nearby September was boosted by a firmer tone in the cash basis market, they said.
Soybeans closed two to 17-1/2 cents per bushel higher, with September up 17-1/2 at $8.15-1/4.
November closed 15-1/2 cents higher at $7.95-3/4 a bushel. November in late dealings broke above resistance at $7.85 and again at $7.90 and buy stops were triggered during each event.

Refco Inc bought four million bushels of November, traders said. Merrill Lynch Futures, Smith Barney, Griffin Trading and Continental Grain each bought one million bushels of November, floor sources said.
The rally was relatively quiet and volume was not extremely heavy which led to possibly exacerbated moves in the market.
"There was very small and light participation in the market right now so they are very volatile," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.
Estimated volume for soybean futures was 47,000 contracts, down from 49,459, according to the CBOT.
In soybean options, Farmers Commodities Corp bought 400 November $9.00 calls at 4-1/4 cents.
Soybean options volume was estimated at 20,000 contracts, down from 20,683 Wednesday.

Position squaring also was noted before the expected release of a Leslie/ADM Elevator Survey Friday and before an expected release of Sparks Companies crop numbers late Thursday or Friday, the traders said.
